digest.en: Russia’s air campaign intensifies over Kyiv, forcing survivors from a destroyed building while Ukraine tests AI-powered drones in response. Meanwhile, the EU tightens border controls to restrict Russian entry, and Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis frames recent AI hacks as early warning shots for the industry.
digest.hi: न्यूयॉर्क में एक भारतीय युवक के नाम पर कानून बनाने की प्रक्रिया शुरू हो गई है। इसी बीच जयशंकर ने चीन को सीमा पर शांति के बिना रिश्ते नहीं रखने का दो-टूक जवाब दिया।

articles.title: Girls In Hijabs Turned Away From Azerbaijani Schools Amid Protests Over Dress Code
articles.summary: Azerbaijani parents and students protested after schools barred girls wearing hijabs from classes. The dispute followed a new ban on clothing deemed incompatible with secular education. The move has intensified friction between religious families and state policy. A new dress-code dispute in Azerbaijan’s public schools has sparked protests by parents and students after reports that girls wearing hijabs, or Islamic headscarf, were turned away from classes.

articles.title: Google DeepMind’s Hassabis calls AI hacks ‘early warning shots’
articles.summary: Demis Hassabis described recent AI security breaches as early warning shots. He argued the field needs best practices similar to those in biology or nuclear sectors. He also called for an international standards body to secure critical AI systems. Demis Hassabis said there ⁠was “a lot of work to do” to adopt the kind of best practices that other fields such as biology or the nuclear sector use to secure critical ​systems and that some sort of ‌international standards body would eventually be needed.

articles.title: Ukraine Tests AI-Powered Drones As Debate Grows Over Autonomous Weapons
articles.summary: Ukraine is deploying artificial intelligence in drones to track and engage targets. Military officials confirm humans retain control over lethal decisions. Developers caution that fully autonomous weapons systems are approaching operational reality on the battlefield. Ukraine is increasingly using artificial intelligence in drones and other battlefield systems to track, identify, and attack targets. Military officials say humans still remain in control of lethal decisions, but developers warn that fully autonomous weapons are moving closer to reality.

articles.title: Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns
articles.summary: Guinea-Bissau's health minister stated the government did not authorize a Danish-led hepatitis B trial in newborns. The study, backed by the US government and private partners, would not test vaccine safety or effectiveness. The ministry denied approval for the controversial research. Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK JrGuinea-Bissau has not approved the controversial hepatitis B study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday. The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would inst.

articles.title: EU Working On Multiple Fronts To Limit Russians From Entering Bloc
articles.summary: The European Union is developing measures to restrict Russian citizens from entering the bloc. Officials are considering a total ban on non-essential travel into the Schengen zone. These efforts aim to limit movement across multiple policy fronts. The European Union is working on multiple fronts to limit the number of Russian citizens that can enter the bloc, including the nuclear option of a total ban on all non-essential travel into the club’s Schengen zone.

articles.title: Gaza braces for winter amid attacks, joint patrols in CAR, 90 cities commit to sustainable
articles.summary: The UN and partners are preparing for winter in Gaza despite ongoing attacks on civilians. OCHA highlighted the urgent need for cold and rainy season support. Humanitarian efforts continue amid persistent violence and displacement in the territory. The UN and its partners are stepping up preparations in Gaza for the approaching cold and rainy season, even as attacks affecting civilians continue, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said on Wednesday.

articles.title: Cholera cases spike amid fight against Ebola
articles.summary: The WHO reported over 125,000 suspected cholera cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The epidemic has caused 3,644 suspected deaths since January 2025. This surge occurs while the country simultaneously battles an ongoing Ebola outbreak. The cholera epidemic continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 125,000 suspected cases and 3,644 suspected deaths were recorded between January 2025 and the end of September 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Wednesday.

articles.title: WFP warns of potential ‘humanitarian catastrophe’ as fighting blocks aid delivery
articles.summary: The UN World Food Programme warned of a humanitarian catastrophe in Yemen. Intensifying fighting has cut off life-saving assistance to 800,000 people. Blocked roads and shifting frontlines severely restrict access to Taiz and other conflict zones. Intensifying fighting in Yemen has cut off life-saving assistance to 800,000 people as shifting frontlines, blocked roads and growing insecurity severely restrict access to the city of Taiz and other conflict zones, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) said on Wednesday.

articles.title: Survivors Rescued From Kyiv Building After Deadly Russian Strike
articles.summary: Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv overnight, killing three people and injuring over twenty others. Survivors were rescued from a damaged building. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Western partners provided no advance warning of the attack, highlighting a gap in intelligence sharing. Moscow launched a wave of ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv overnight, killing at least three people and injuring more than 20.

articles.title: Ukrainians Brace For The Worst Amid Russia's Escalating Air Campaign
articles.summary: Russia continues its aerial campaign against Ukrainian infrastructure, targeting apartment buildings, bridges, and power plants. As winter approaches, Kyiv residents are preparing for potential outages. The sustained attacks on the electricity grid aim to degrade civilian resilience during the colder months. Russia shows no sign of letting up on its escalating aerial campaign against Ukraine’s apartment buildings, bridges, power plants, electricity grid, and other targets.

articles.title: US Navy’s SSN(X) won’t arrive for years as China closes sub gap
articles.summary: The US Navy issued a sources-sought notice for its next-generation SSN(X) attack submarine. This move addresses the aging fleet while China closes the undersea gap. Chinese shipyards now offer superior capacity and acoustic stealth, challenging American naval dominance in the region. As the US Navy lays the groundwork for its next-generation SSN(X) attack submarine to replace its aging fleet, the US’s longstanding undersea supremacy faces an intensifying test against China’s rapid naval buildup, advancing acoustic stealth and superior shipyard capacity.

articles.title: 'We'll Keep Waiting': Afghanistan's Dead-End Road To China
articles.summary: Satellite imagery confirms the Taliban completed a road to the China-Afghanistan border. Beijing shows no signs of opening the militarized boundary. The infrastructure project remains a dead end for trade routes. Satellite imagery sourced by RFE/RL confirms Taliban claims they have completed a road that leads up to China's remote border with Afghanistan. However there is no indication Beijing intends to open the militarized boundary any time soon.

articles.title: Indonesia wildfire fuelled by El Niño razes almost 300 homes
articles.summary: An El Niño-fueled wildfire on Sumatra island destroyed nearly 300 homes in Bangka Belitung province. Hundreds of residents evacuated as shifting winds drove the blaze toward settlements. The incident adds to the country’s ongoing battle with devastating blazes and haze. Hundreds of people displaced in Bangka Belitung province as shift in wind direction drove blaze towards settlementA forest fire on Indonesia’s Sumatra island fuelled by El Niño has razed nearly 300 homes, forcing hundreds of people to evacuate, an official said on Tuesday as the country battles devastating blazes and haze. Residents first spotted the fire approaching their village in Bangka Belitun.

articles.title: How Ukraine's Strikes On Data Centers Disrupted Taxis, Shopping, And Business In Russia And Beyond
articles.summary: Ukrainian drones hit three Yandex data centers. Repairs will take months. The strikes disrupted taxi services, online shopping, and business operations across Russia and other countries where the tech firm operates. Ukrainian drone strikes on three data centers operated by Russia’s Yandex will reportedly take months to repair and have caused widespread disruption in everyday life across Russia and other countries the sprawling tech company operates in.

articles.title: 800 million young people face a future without jobs
articles.summary: The UNDP head warned 800 million young people in developing economies will lack jobs. This projection covers the coming years without immediate action. The agency launched two initiatives to boost investment and employment. 800 million young people face a future without jobs.

articles.title: ‘Need for UN has never been greater,’ UN chief says, proposing slimmer $3.3 billion budget for 2027
articles.summary: António Guterres proposed a $3.3 billion budget for 2027. This represents a $40.8 million cut from previous plans. He cited climate disruption, AI, war, and hunger as drivers for the need. Amid climate disruption, an AI revolution, war and growing hunger, “the need for the United Nations has never been greater,” Secretary-General António Guterres said on Tuesday, presenting a $3.3 billion programme budget proposal for next year – a cut of $40.8 million.

articles.title: Germany Starts Nord Stream 'War Crime' Trial With Prosecutors Blaming Ukrainian 'State Authorities'
articles.summary: German prosecutors will begin a war crime trial regarding the Nord Stream pipeline explosions. The case marks the first public, sworn testimony on the incident after years of speculation. Prosecutors are blaming Ukrainian state actors for the sabotage. After four years of speculation, leaks, and briefings by anonymous sources, the world is finally about to hear evidence given publicly under oath in a German courtroom about how the Nord Stream gas pipelines were blown up -- in a case that could prove politically explosive.

articles.title: Latin American organised crime ‘may operate in 16 European countries’
articles.summary: Latin American organised crime groups may now operate in sixteen European countries. A Guardian investigation links the fivefold rise in cocaine seizures to these expanding networks. Cartels have established deep roots across the continent over the last decade. Cocaine seizures in Europe are up more than fivefold in 10 years as a host of cartels take root. A four-month Guardian investigation reveals the true scale of a continent-wide shiftA four-month investigation by the Guardian has revealed that the surge in cocaine trafficking to Europe is directly linked to the expanding presence of Latin American criminal networks in Europe, where they have forged.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Accuses Russia Of Breaking Trump's Cease-Fire On Energy Strikes
articles.summary: Trump defended allowing Russian diesel exports despite criticism from Ukraine, Europe, and Republicans. He claimed an energy cease-fire exists between Kyiv and Moscow. Neither side has confirmed the arrangement. The move drew sharp backlash from allied governments and domestic opponents. US President Donald Trump, in the face of sharp criticism from officials in Ukraine, Europe, and even his Republican party, defended his decision to allow Russian diesel exports and insisted an energy cease-fire between Kyiv and Moscow is in place despite a lack of confirmation from either side.

articles.title: Pulling Ethiopia and Eritrea Back from War
articles.summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea are edging closer to direct conflict, threatening stability in the Horn of Africa and Red Sea basin. Diplomatic efforts remain active to avert disaster. The situation risks escalating regional mayhem if tensions between Addis Ababa and Asmara continue to intensify. Addis Ababa and Asmara are edging closer to a direct conflict, which would cause further mayhem in the troubled Horn of Africa and the Red Sea basin.

articles.title: Colombia peace deal must endure as insecurity grows, Security Council hears
articles.summary: The UN representative in Colombia stated the peace deal must endure despite growing insecurity. The agreement ended a decades-long insurgency nearly ten years ago. Rising violence threatens the stability of the accord. The official emphasized the need to prevent the deal from faltering. Nearly 10 years after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement to end a decades-long insurgency, the deal is under strain from growing insecurity – and the UN’s top official in the country says it cannot be allowed to falter.

articles.title: Controversial vaccine trial touted by RFK Jr gets go-ahead in Guinea-Bissau
articles.summary: Guinea-Bissau approved a controversial trial to withhold hepatitis B vaccines from thousands of newborns. Danish researchers will conduct the study. It aligns with the vaccine vision of US Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Recommended dose of hepatitis B vaccine will be withheld from thousands of newborns by Danish researchersA controversial research trial that will withhold hepatitis B vaccines from some African newborns was given approval to move forward this week. It is a central part of the vaccine vision for Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime.

articles.title: How Close Are Ethiopia and Eritrea to All-out War?
articles.summary: Crisis Group’s Alan Boswell discussed the fighting in Ethiopia’s Tigray region on Hold Your Fire. He analyzed the risk of direct war between Ethiopia and Eritrea. The conversation covered factors that might prevent further escalation in the Horn of Africa. In this episode of Hold Your Fire!, Richard is joined by Crisis Group’s Horn of Africa director, Alan Boswell, to discuss the fighting in Ethiopia’s Tigray region, the risk of direct war between Ethiopia and Eritrea and what may prevent further escalation.

articles.title: Toward a Thaw in the Cambodia-Thailand Border Conflict
articles.summary: Hostilities between Cambodia and Thailand ceased in late 2025 after two rounds of combat. The truce now faces growing strain. To prevent further war, both nations should restore normal diplomatic ties. They must also resume work on demarcating their shared border. Hostilities between Cambodia and Thailand ceased in late 2025, after two rounds of combat along the frontier. But the truce is under growing strain.

articles.title: On Our Radar
articles.summary: Crisis Group’s On Our Radar weekly scan highlights global conflicts and crises. Field experts explain why specific hotspots matter or what actions are needed. The report covers both under-reported trends and major developments. On Our Radar scans conflicts and crises around the globe every week and features some of the hotspots Crisis Group’s analysts are closely watching. Whether an under-reported trend or a headline-grabbing development, our field experts explain why it matters or what should be done.

articles.title: एयर फ्रांस ने पाकिस्तान समेत 31 देशों के पायलटों पर लगाया बैन, जानें क्यों नहीं रहा यहां के
articles.summary: एयर फ्रांस ने इजराइल से कूटनीतिक संबंध न रखने वाले 31 देशों के पायलटों पर बैन लगाया। यह कदम फ्लाईदुबई की सुरक्षा घटना और पाकिस्तानी पायलटों के लाइसेंस विवाद के बाद उठा गया। फ्लाईदुबई की फ्लाइट में ओमानी को-पायलट की 9/11 जैसी खौफनाक साजिश सामने आने के बाद इजराइल ने एयर सिक्योरिटी बहुत सख्त कर दी है. इजराइल के नए नियमों को मानते हुए एअर फ्रांस ने पाकिस्तान समेत उन 31 देशों के पायलटों और क्रू पर बैन लगा दिया है, जिनके इजराइल से कूटनीतिक रिश्ते नहीं हैं.

articles.summary: अभिजीत दीपके पर दिल्ली एयरपोर्ट पर एक शख्स ने हमला किया। आरोपी ने उन्हें सीआईए एजेंट कहकर देश को बर्बाद करने का आरोप लगाया। कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) के संस्थापक अभिजीत दीपके के बुधवार दोपहर दिल्ली एयरपोर्ट पहुंचते ही भारी हंगामे का सामना करना पड़ा. सौरव दास और आशुतोष रांका को 5 दिन की न्यायिक हिरासत में भेजे जाने के बाद दीपके दिल्ली पहुंचे तो एयरपोर्ट से बाहर निकलते वक्त एक शख्स ने उनसे कहा, 'देश क्यों बर्बाद कर रहे हो?' इसके बाद वह शख्स दीपके पर चिल्लाने लगा.

articles.summary: प्रवर्तन निदेशालय ने तिरुपति लड्डू में मिलावट के मामले में मनी लॉन्ड्रिंग के संदेह पर जांच शुरू की है। हैदराबाद ज़ोनल ऑफिस ने PMLA के तहत भोले बाबा ऑर्गेनिक डेयरीमिल्क और श्री वैष्णवी डेयरी स्पेशलिटीज समेत कई कंपनियों और उनके प्रमोटरों के खिलाफ कार्रवाई की है। प्रवर्तन निदेशालय (ED) के हैदराबाद जोनल ऑफिस ने 'मनी लॉन्ड्रिंग रोकथाम अधिनियम (PMLA), 2002' के तहत M/s भोले बाबा ऑर्गेनिक डेयरीमिल्क प्राइवेट लिमिटेड और M/s श्री वैष्णवी डेयरी स्पेशलिटीज प्राइवेट लिमिटेड, उनके प्रमोटर विपिन जैन और पोमिल जैन और उनके परिवार के सदस्यों, M/s सुकृति फूड्स प्राइवेट लिमिटेड, उसके प्रमोटर कैलाश चंद मंगला और उनके परिवार के सदस्यों और अन्य संबंधित संस्थाओं/व्यक्तियों की 12।

articles.title: क्या कन्हैया कुमार की राह पर चलेंगी नेहा बोरा? कांग्रेस पर खुद दिया जवाब
articles.summary: इंडिया गठबंधन के विरोध प्रदर्शन में AISA अध्यक्ष नेहा बोरा ने CEC ज्ञानेश कुमार को हटाने की मांग उठाई। राहुल गांधी ने कांग्रेस पर हुए हमले का जवाब देते हुए पार्टी की नीति पर स्पष्टता प्रदान की। लोकसभा में नेता विपक्ष राहुल गांधी ने दिल्ली में इंडिया गठबंधन के सहयोगी दलों के साथ बहुत बड़ा विरोध प्रदर्शन किया. इस विरोध प्रदर्शन में इंडिया ब्लॉक के सहयोगी पार्टियों के नेता और कार्यकर्ता बड़ी संख्या में शामिल हुए, लेकिन प्रदर्शन में राजनीतिक दलों के नेताओं के बीच ऑल इंडिया स्टूडेंट्स एसोसिएशन (AISA) की राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष नेहा बोरा ने सोशल मीडिया पर काफी सुर्खियां बटोरी.

articles.summary: स्पेसएक्स ने ट्रंप-पुतिन समझौते के बाद यूक्रेन में स्टारलिंक की स्पीड रोक दी। इससे काउंटर-ड्रोन ऑपरेशन्स और मोर्चे की सुरक्षा को भारी नुकसान हुआ। अमेरिका में चुनाव और डीजल की कीमतों पर काबू पाने के लिए यूक्रेन पर दबाव बनाया जा रहा है। डोनाल्ड ट्रंप और व्लादिमीर पुतिन की सीक्रेट डील के बाद मस्क की कंपनी स्पेसएक्स ने यूक्रेन में स्टारलिंक की स्पीड रोक दी है.

articles.summary: पाकिस्तानी सेना ने बलूचिस्तान में आतंकवाद विरोधी अभियान चलाया। इस कार्रवाई में पाँच आतंकियों को ढेर किया गया। प्रांत में उग्रवाद और अपराधों के कारण कानून व्यवस्था चरमरा चुकी है, जिसके सुधार के लिए सेना लगातार अभियान चला रही है। पाकिस्तान (Pakistan) का बलूचिस्तान (Balochistan) प्रांत देश में आतंकवाद के मामले में दूसरे नंबर पर है। बलूचिस्तान में आतंकवाद ही नहीं, उग्रवाद और अन्य अपराधों की वजह से भी कानून व्यवस्था चरमरा चुकी है।

articles.summary: फॉकलैंड द्वीप समूह में तेल और गैस के भंडार के कारण ब्रिटेन और अर्जेंटीना के बीच तनाव बढ़ा। अर्जेंटीना के राष्ट्रपति जेवियर माइली की धमकियों के बाद ब्रिटेन ने द्वीपों पर सैन्य तैयारी बढ़ाई। वहाँ 100 से अधिक सैनिकों की सीक्रेट ट्रेनिंग शुरू की गई है। फॉकलैंड द्वीप समूह में तेल और गैस का भारी खजाना छुपा है. इसी वजह से ब्रिटेन और अर्जेंटीना में एक बार फिर जंग जैसा तनाव बन गया है.

articles.summary: अमेरिका में सितंबर महीने में महंगाई दर 3.7 प्रतिशत तक पहुँची। पेट्रोल की कीमतें साल भर में 34 प्रतिशत बढ़ीं, जिससे उपभोक्ता कीमतों में भारी उछाल आया। बढ़ती ईंधन लागत ने पूरी महंगाई का आंकड़ा ऊपर उठा दिया है। अमेरिका में महंगाई काफी बढ़ गई है। सितंबर महीने में उपभोक्ता कीमतों में भारी उछाल देखने को मिला है। पेट्रोल के दाम भी बहुत बढ़ गए और इसी वजह से पूरी महंगाई का आंकड़ा ऊपर चला गया है।

articles.title: अमेरिकी टैक्सपेयर के पैसे की रिसर्च पर चीन की नजर: US हाउस कमिटी ने SIRA एक्ट पास करने की लगाई गुहार
articles.summary: अमेरिकी हाउस की सिलेक्ट कमिटी ने SIRA एक्ट को जल्द पास करने की अपील की है। कमिटी का मानना है कि चीनी कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी से जुड़े खतरों को रोकने के लिए यह कदम जरूरी है। इससे टैक्सपेयर के पैसे से होने वाली रिसर्च की चोरी रोकी जा सकेगी। कमिटी का मानना है कि अमेरिकी टैक्सपेयर्स के पैसे से होने वाली रिसर्च और इनोवेशन की चोरी को रोकने के लिए यह सख्त कदम उठाना बेहद जरू।

articles.title: सड़ी-गली लकड़ियां पचाकर साढ़े 6 करोड़ साल से जिंदा है, डायनासोर के खात्मे के ठीक बाद धरती पर पनपा
articles.summary: चीन के युन्नान में साइंटिस्ट्स ने डायनासोर के बाद पनपी विशाल फंगस की खोज की। इसे डायनजुनस रेक्स नाम दिया गया है। यह 50 सेंटीमीटर ऊंची और 2.2 किलोग्राम भारी है। डीएनए विश्लेषण से पता चला कि यह मृत लकड़ियों से उत्पन्न हुई। चीन के युन्नान प्रांत के जंगलों में साइंटिस्ट्स ने एक विशालकाय फंगस की खोज की है. इसे डायनजुनस रेक्स या डी-रेक्स नाम दिया गया है, जो करीब साढ़े 6 करोड़ साल से छिपा हुआ था.
